clue.text: Absurd sketch Rothko initially disowned

indicators.note: a letter disowned is cast off, so it is taken out of the sketch

parts.note: a draft is a rough sketch of a design or text

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the painter's name

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a ridiculous drawing that Mark Rothko has refused to own as his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from Rothko, and 'disowned' removes it from DRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is informal British for silly or foolish, a close synonym of absurd.

clue.text: Lord, being risen, Bacon cut for band of clergy

indicators.note: in a down clue being risen means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the Lord is God
collar is a cut of bacon from the pig's neck

explanation.surface: An Easter picture of the risen Lord, with bacon sliced for a clerical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' seems to be Francis Bacon the painter, but a cut of bacon is COLLAR. 'band' is a strip of material, not a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog collar is the stiff white band worn round the neck by members of the clergy.

clue.text: Leave military formation in radioactive dust cloud

definitions.meaning: to ... is to leave the ranks when dismissed on parade
radioactive dust spread after a nuclear explosion

explanation.surface: Soldiers break ranks inside a deadly nuclear cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall out is the parade order to break ranks; fallout is debris spread by a nuclear blast.

clue.text: Line taken with infant making incomprehensible sounds

parts.note: a babe is a baby or infant

explanation.surface: A baby on a phone line is making noises nobody can understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A babel is a confused noise of many voices, after the biblical tower where speech was confounded.

clue.text: Dramatist in France good about orders I ignored

indicators.note: about means around, so the French word goes round the rest

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter I is removed

parts.note: enjoins means commands or orders

explanation.surface: A playwright in France is good at handling commands, but someone is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes the I from the word for orders before 'about' wraps the French word around it; 'In France' is part of the French-word leaf, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson was an English Renaissance playwright, author of Volpone and The Alchemist.

clue.text: By it one develops feeling for character

definitions.text: By it one develops feeling for character

parts.words: By it one develops feeling for character
parts.note: the surface suggests building empathy; really it is a raised script read by touching each letter

explanation.surface: A method that teaches empathy and understanding of personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeling for character' reads as sensitivity to personality; literally it is feeling a written character with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-dot writing system for blind readers lets them identify each letter by touch.

clue.text: Tricked 500 in Spanish city

indicators.note: in places the Roman number inside the city name

parts.note: Leon is a city in north-west Spain
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone was fooled out of five hundred in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: To be led on is to be deceived or lured into believing something false.

clue.text: American journey without end lacking interest

indicators.note: without end means the last letter of the journey word is dropped

parts.note: a ride is a journey on a horse or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: An American trip that never finishes and holds no excitement for anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid describes something dry and dull, so a lecture or book lacking interest can be called arid.

clue.text: Castle hit — destroyed for sport

indicators.note: a castle destroyed is broken apart, so its letters with hit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A castle was struck and wrecked for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics covers track and field events such as running and jumping, a sport.

clue.text: Sounding bell after time's gone is hint

indicators.note: gone means removed, so the time letter disappears

parts.note: a bell sounding lightly makes a tinkling
T is an abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bell ringing once time is up gives a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suspicion or hint of something.

clue.text: Award one in Drake's ship's exchanged for a fish

indicators.note: exchanged for says one letter is swapped out and the next piece put in its place

parts.note: Sir Francis Drake sailed round the world in the Golden Hind; the possessive adds an S
I is the Roman numeral one
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A prize on board Drake's famous vessel gets traded for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in Drake's ship's' is the I of HIND; 'exchanged for' swaps it for A, giving GOLDEN HANDS before HAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a generous lump-sum payment granted to someone leaving a job, a kind of award.

clue.text: Cricketing pair seen outside harbour town and city

indicators.note: seen outside says the pair sits around the town, one letter each side

parts.note: in cricket a pair is two ducks, scores of nought in both innings, shown as two Os
a port is a harbour town

explanation.surface: Two cricketers are spotted outside a coastal town and a larger city.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a pair means a batter out for nought (a duck) in both innings, so it gives O and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto, also called Porto, is a major city in northern Portugal famous for port wine.

clue.text: Spice Girl appears in rank undergarments

indicators.note: appears in places the Spice Girl inside the rank

parts.note: a rank is a line, as of soldiers
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls pop group

explanation.surface: A pop singer turns up in some foul-smelling underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like smelly, but here it is a row, LINE. The Spice Girls were a 1990s British girl band; Geri was one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes, so it covers undergarments.

clue.text: Meet wayward son in shelter I need to check

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters with the son inside the shelter word

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind

indicators.note: wayward means going astray, so the letters of meet are rearranged

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A rebellious son is to be met under cover, and someone wants to verify it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' scrambles the four letters of 'Meet', and 'in' puts that jumble plus the son letter between the first and second letters of the shelter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Let me see is what someone says when pausing to think or asking to look, much like saying they need to check.

clue.text: Tree bark used by settlers

definitions.meaning: a name for the hawthorn tree, which blossoms in May
a bark or barque is a sailing ship; the ... carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620

explanation.surface: Pioneers used the bark of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' suggests tree bark but means a ship, a barque.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayflower names hawthorn blossom and also the ship that took the Pilgrim settlers to New England.

clue.text: Wince in embarrassment where church welcomes cartel

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the cartel goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
a ring is a group of people colluding, like a cartel

explanation.surface: People squirm with shame at a church that opens its doors to a criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to shrink or flinch with awkwardness, which is wincing from embarrassment.

clue.text: Famous boxer had to work hand in glove

parts.note: Henry Cooper was a much-loved British heavyweight boxer
to have a meal is to eat it, so had means ate

explanation.surface: A famous fighter had to work closely in his boxing glove.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a 1960s British heavyweight boxing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Working hand in glove means working closely together, which is to cooperate.

clue.text: Redesigned garden set apart

indicators.note: redesigned means laid out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden laid out again stands separate from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged people are separated and living apart, no longer close.

clue.text: Publish that American author

parts.note: a newspaper runs a story when it publishes it
yon is an old or dialect word meaning that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: An editor tells staff to print the work of a certain US writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American writer of Broadway stories, the basis of Guys and Dolls.

clue.text: Plain's high point with river feeding reservoir

parts.note: up means at a high point

indicators.note: feeding means flowing into, so the river letter goes inside the reservoir

parts.note: a font is the basin holding water for baptism in a church

explanation.surface: A plain's highest spot has a river flowing into a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like flat land but means frank. A font is the water basin in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Upfront means frank and honest, as plain-speaking people are.

clue.text: Wander around with mum before books launch

parts.note: to moon around is to wander about aimlessly
keep mum means stay silent, and SH is the call for silence
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone strolls about with their mother before a new book is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means quiet, hence SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonshot is the launch of a spacecraft to the moon, and by extension any ambitious venture.

clue.text: Friend coming round is first to see painter

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the friend word encloses the rest

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A friend visiting is the first to see a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist, a leading figure of modern painting.

clue.text: Legal process shows sense

definitions.meaning: a session of a court or tribunal

explanation.surface: A court proceeding shows good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing is a trial or inquiry in court; hearing is also the faculty of perceiving sound.

clue.text: Loaded a firearm at the front — easy

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of the weapon word

parts.note: fluent speech or writing is easy and flowing

explanation.surface: A gun is loaded at the front, which makes things easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' seems to describe the firearm; it is slang for rich, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very rich, and affluent means wealthy.

clue.text: Key frequently used to get in

definitions.meaning: A much-pressed key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A key is often used to get inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter is a keyboard key pressed constantly; to enter also means to come in.

clue.text: Start with alcohol and Jack on about bloomers!

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the sailor and concerning words are read backwards

parts.note: jack and tar are both slang words for a sailor
re means on or concerning, as in letters

indicators.note: start with points to the opening letter of the drink word

explanation.surface: An exclamation about drinking with a sailor and mentioning ladies' knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TAR and RE to make ERRAT; 'Start with' takes A from alcohol. Bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers, but here a bloomer is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is British slang for a mistake, and errata are listed errors in a printed work.

clue.text: Though a smart cookie, also involved in drunken nights

parts.note: a smart cookie is a clever person, so no twit

indicators.note: involved in puts the word for also inside the jumbled letters
drunken signals that the letters of nights stagger into a new order

parts.note: and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Despite being clever, someone gets caught up in nights of heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A smart cookie is no twit. 'drunken' scrambles the six letters of 'nights', and 'involved in' sets the word for also among them, after the first three.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding can be used as a conjunction meaning although, so it can replace though.

clue.text: Large body will need tons crammed into short dress

indicators.note: crammed into means squeezed inside, so the tons letter goes within
short means the garment word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a sari is a South Asian dress

explanation.surface: A big person has to squeeze a lot into a skimpy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SARI to SAR; 'crammed into' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a huge celestial body such as the sun.

clue.text: Super Kent player always around to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve means to keep within, so the energy letter is held inside
around here means turned round, so the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A superb Kent cricketer is always circling around to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses EVER into REVE; 'to conserve' keeps E inside it. 'Kent' suggests the English county; it is Clark Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Reeve played Superman, whose everyday identity is Clark Kent, in the films.

clue.text: My word once accepted by renegade

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the answer sits within the last word

explanation.surface: A traitor takes on an old oath of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic mild oath, an old-fashioned exclamation like my word.
